newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 10.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- The government will allow private companies to participate in electric power and industrial complex projects on the same terms as public firms, which previously dominated such undertakings.

- Three mushroom pickers were found killed, two men shot and a woman strangled, on a mountainside close to the area being searched by South Korean troops for fleeing North Korean armed guerrillas. The victims are presumed to have been killed by the agents.

- Government announces it will freeze wages and other personnel costs in public companies and reduce the number of public servants by 10,000 over four years in a move to shore up national competitiveness.

- South Korea demands an apology from Pyongyang for the recent submarine infiltration incident, along with a promise not to repeat such provocation. The demand will be presented as a precondition for economic cooperation with the North and assistance for light-water nuclear power project during Friday's meeting with U.S. assistant secretary of state Winston Lord.
- Army troops found the bodies of three mushroom pickers, two shot to death and another strangled. The three are presumed to have been killed by fleeing North Korean agents.

- The government plans to lay off 10,000 public servants over four years, and is also shooting for an average 25 percent cut in the prices of industrial land. These are part of a package of measures to boost national competitiveness by 10 percent.
- Three civilians found killed, probably by fleeing North Korean agents. Empty M-16 cartridges were found near the bodies, and the manhunt for North Korean agents has been stepped up.

- Big corporations will be allowed foreign commercial loans and will be given access to foreign-currency loans provided by domestic banks. The government also plans to cut 10,000 government jobs over the next four years to boost productivity.
